experiment: Per-layer score-temperature (magnitude) calibration of SLHA compressed attention
question: Is the SLHA compressed-score quality gap primarily caused by a layer-dependent score-magnitude mismatch, equivalent to an incorrect softmax temperature?
conclusion: Per-layer and global multiplicative calibration recovered less than 1% of the PPL gap, while fitted scales remained close to identity and scaling removed less than approximately 1% of raw-score error. No positive rescaling that is constant within a softmax row -- per-layer, per-head, per-query-row, or context-length-dependent -- can close the gap: every such rescaling is exactly rank-preserving, the measured optimum of the global sweep sits at a ~ 1.0, and even attributing 100% of the score residual to per-row gain jitter prices that whole family at only a few percent of the gap. The quality gap is therefore dominated by score distortion that is NOT constant within a softmax row. This experiment does not further decompose that residual into reordering versus order-preserving gap error.

provenance.note: screening ran at 4 chunks because this host is materially slower; every control used the same chunk count, so within-experiment deltas are consistent

seam_audit.qwen25_specifics: arch != GROK, attn_soft_cap = false, kq_b = null, no ALiBi
seam_audit.additive_offset_note: softmax(x+b) == softmax(x), so an additive per-layer offset is a softmax no-op; means are reported as a diagnostic only

fit_dataset_provenance.positions_included: k <= t AND k < n_written (causal prefix, tiles present)
fit_dataset_provenance.masked_exclusion_argument: Perplexity chunks start at position 0, so query token t attends keys 0..t. k <= t is therefore a strict subset of the causally-unmasked key set; no softmax-masked key can enter the fit.
fit_dataset_provenance.padding_exclusion_argument: kq->ne[0] (n_kv) is padded to >= 256 by llama_kv_cache::get_n_kv. The fit clamps kmax to n_written (tiles actually encoded), so padded positions (baseline exactly 0, no tile data) never contribute.
fit_dataset_provenance.robust_eps_meaning: pairs with |b| <= eps or |s| <= eps are excluded from the ROBUST median-ratio estimator only (unstable ratio); OLS and variance-matching use every finite pair
fit_dataset_provenance.domination_verdict: no degenerate subpopulation dominates the fit

local_curve_and_resolution.note: the binary is deterministic (identical configs give bit-identical PPL), so this roughness is not measurement noise but genuine chaotic sensitivity of the forward pass; it is the resolution floor for recovered-gap claims

pooled_aggregate_caveat.caveat: A pooled OLS across layers is NOT a meaningful aggregate: layer 0 alone carries 99.91% of the pooled sum(s^2), so the pooled value essentially reports that one layer's scale. The per-layer values are the meaningful quantity; the pooled number is reported only with this caveat and is not used as evidence.

scale_family_exclusion_bound.argument: softmax normalizes over one (layer, head, query) row, so a per-layer, per-head, per-row or context-length-dependent positive scale is constant within the normalization group. Every such scale is exactly rank-preserving, and scaling the raw score equals scaling the row-centred logit because the row-constant part is discarded by softmax. So one global sweep probes the whole family's mean, and the residual bounds its spread.
scale_family_exclusion_bound.sigma_a_definition: std_b*sqrt(1-r^2)/rms(s): the per-row gain jitter that would be needed to produce the observed residual if 100% of it were magnitude jitter -- a deliberate over-estimate
scale_family_exclusion_bound.curvature_step: quadratic fit over the local window

affine_control.rationale: softmax(x+c)==softmax(x): a constant offset cannot change attention, so the slope is the only magnitude parameter that matters. Reported both through the origin and with a free intercept to rule out an affine confound.
affine_control.verdict: both estimators put the magnitude relationship within ~1% of identity at every layer, so the near-unit scale is not an artifact of forcing the fit through the origin

scale_stability.structure_note: the split-half disagreement (max 0.0256) is AS LARGE AS or LARGER than the entire per-layer spread of the fitted scale (0.0208), so the apparent per-layer structure is NOT resolved: the per-layer scales are consistent with all layers sharing a scale of ~1.0 plus estimation noise. This makes the fitted per-layer scale files perturbations of the identity rather than a genuine search over per-layer temperatures, and it is why they are reported alongside, not instead of, the direct global sweep. Rank correlation between the two disjoint halves is 0.354.

magnitude_vs_ranking.rule: magnitude_dominant: top1 >= 0.90 AND sse_reduction >= 0.20; ranking_dominant: top1 < 0.90 AND sse_reduction < 0.05; mixed: top1 < 0.90 AND sse_reduction >= 0.05; else unresolved

invariance_under_positive_scaling.claim: for a>0, argmax(a*s)=argmax(s), the top-k set is preserved, and cosine(a*s,b)=cosine(s,b)
invariance_under_positive_scaling.scope_licensed: no positive scale that is constant within a softmax row -- per-layer, per-head, per-query-row, or context-length-dependent -- can change WHICH key wins within that row, with that row's inputs held fixed
scope_NOT_licensed: scaling is NOT an end-to-end no-op: softmax(a*s) != softmax(s), so attention weights, the layer output, and every downstream layer's Q/K change (PPL=270 at a=0.40 proves it)

a positive scale DOES change how much damage a wrong ordering causes: flattening is a hedge against a noisy ranker, so a<1 was a priori a live remedy that algebra alone cannot exclude -- only the empirical sweep closes that channel
invariance is local: scaling layer L can change layer L+1's ordering

magnitude_vs_ranking.ranking_metric_caveat: top-1/top-5/cosine come from the shadow-mode add_vector call, which compares the FULL n_kv row including causally-masked keys, unlike the magnitude fit which clamps to k<=t. They are therefore NOT clean attention-relevant rank-agreement numbers, and the per-layer classification below inherits that limitation. They are also shadow-only, so they structurally cannot respond to SLHA_SCORE_SCALE.
magnitude_vs_ranking.not_decomposed: This experiment excludes the row-constant scale family. It does NOT separate reordering from order-preserving gap errors: a monotone nonlinear magnitude map is non-scalar, order-preserving, changes the softmax distribution, and is invisible to every statistic computed here. A per-KEY magnitude error is likewise a magnitude defect that is not row-constant and therefore does change ranking.

identity_controls.note: all three replacement identity variants must resolve to scale 1.0 on every layer and agree within run-to-run variability; the scale interface must not alter score semantics at identity

determinism.finding: with the dst zero-init race fixed, numerically identical replacement configurations return bit-identical perplexity, so any difference between scale strategies is signal rather than run-to-run noise
determinism.passthrough_unaffected: 9.3852 both before and after (race was localised to the replace write path)
determinism.consequence: all measurements in this report were taken with the fixed, deterministic binary; the pre-fix rows are retained separately and excluded from every aggregate
determinism.scaled_path_note: the identity controls resolve to a==1.0, which SKIPS the scaling loop entirely (guarded by `a != 1.0`), so they do not exercise the scaled write path. These repeats use genuinely scaled configurations (scaled_vectors>0) and are also bit-identical.

recovered_gap_categories.note: reporting categories, not universal statistical thresholds

discarded_run_policy: runs are excluded from every aggregate if the driver exited non-zero or any strict counter failed (valid != true, active_coverage != 1, error_code != 0, failed/fallback vectors > 0, invalid_scale > 0); invalid scale specs are rejected before a run starts
recommended_next_experiments: joint Q/K projection training (optimize the compressed projection for score ordering)
pairwise ranking loss on score pairs rather than L2 on score values
top-k preservation loss during projection training
residual correction of SLHA scores (learned low-rank correction term)
hybrid exact top-k plus compressed tail scoring
recommended_next_note: after a negative scaling result the next diagnostic should target ranking restoration, not another temperature sweep; none of these are implemented in this PR
